journey.name: Notification permission denied
journey.description:
Covers the denial path of the POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt. The node must keep running even when the user refuses notifications — the foreground service is what syncs the chain, and it must not be gated on a permission the user is free to decline. After Android auto-applies "don't ask again" (two denials), the snackbar's action must switch from "Enable" to "Open settings", because a further request would return denied instantly with no dialog and leave a dead button.
PRECONDITION: the permission must not be granted. Reset it before starting with `adb shell pm revoke com.github.jvsena42.mandacaru android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` followed by `adb shell am force-stop com.github.jvsena42.mandacaru`. Revoking is only meaningful on Android 13+ (API 33); on older devices notifications are granted at install time, so mark every snackbar step SKIPPED rather than FAILED.

actions.action: Revoke the notification permission and force-stop the app (`adb shell pm revoke com.github.jvsena42.mandacaru android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` then `adb shell am force-stop com.github.jvsena42.mandacaru`); if the device is below API 33, SKIP the remaining steps
Launch the Mandacaru app and wait for the splash screen to dismiss (poll until nav_node is present)

Verify the node started despite the missing permission: `adb shell dumpsys activity services com.github.jvsena42.mandacaru` lists FlorestaService as running, and the Node tab shows real values rather than placeholders — node_network reads a network name (e.g. BITCOIN) and node_peer_count is above zero. Do not assert on node_sync_percentage here; it is absent during the header-sync phase. Poll for up to 30 seconds, since peers take a few seconds to connect.
Verify the enable-notifications snackbar (snackbar_enable_notifications) is present
Tap the "Enable" action on the snackbar (by text) and tap "Don't allow" on the system permission dialog (by text)

Verify snackbar_enable_notifications is still present, its action is still "Enable", and its message has escalated to the warning about Android stopping the node and wallets losing access to the Electrum server
Tap the "Enable" action again (by text) and tap "Don't allow" on the system permission dialog a second time — Android now auto-applies "don't ask again"
Verify the snackbar action label has changed to "Open settings" (by text)
Tap "Open settings" (by text) and verify the system app-details settings screen for Mandacaru opens
Enable notifications from that settings screen (open "Notifications" and turn on "All Mandacaru notifications"), then press Back until the app is in the foreground again
Verify snackbar_enable_notifications is gone now that the app has resumed with the permission granted
Revoke the permission again and relaunch the app so the snackbar reappears (poll until snackbar_enable_notifications is present)
Dismiss the snackbar with its ✕ (target the "Dismiss" content-description) and verify snackbar_enable_notifications disappears without the permission being granted
Tap through the Blockchain, Transactions and Settings navigation items and back to nav_node, and verify the snackbar does not come back and the app has not crashed
